BivarOptimalMomentumSystematic momentum with gold regime hedge

A long-only momentum strategy on US large-cap equities with a profitability filter, market regime overlay, and gold (GLD) allocation during bear markets. 336 months of out-of-sample backtesting with daily data. Signal on the 18th trading day, execution on the 19th trading day. No look-ahead bias.

I. Strategy Specification

Signal: 18th trading day of each month (after market close)

  1. Regime check: Is the S&P 500 close above its 250-day simple moving average?
    • NO → Sell all stocks. Buy GLD (SPDR Gold Shares). Hold until next month’s signal day.
    • YES → Proceed to step 2.
  2. Compute momentum for every eligible stock:
    Momentum = 50% × (price / price 126 trading days ago − 1) + 50% × (price / price 252 trading days ago − 1)
  3. Filter universe:
    • Market capitalisation > $10 billion
    • EBIT > 0 (operating profit positive, most recent report)
    • US domestic common stock only
  4. Select top 7 by momentum composite. Equal weight (~14.3% each).
  5. Execute on the 19th trading day: sell positions that left the portfolio, buy new ones.
Why momentum works: Stocks that have risen tend to continue rising. Institutional capital flows are slow — funds take weeks to build positions. Information propagates gradually. Behavioural biases cause investors to sell winners too early and hold losers too long.
Why GLD during bear markets: Gold has near-zero correlation with the momentum strategy. During bear markets, gold averages positive returns while stocks fall. The MA250 regime filter identifies bear markets early — switching to GLD preserves capital and generates positive returns during drawdowns.

X. Why Each Parameter

Momentum blend: 50% × 6-month + 50% × 12-month

Combining two horizons captures both short-term acceleration and medium-term trend. Tested against pure 6m, 9m, 12m, and multiple weighted blends. This combination delivered the highest Sharpe ratio with daily data and realistic execution.

Market cap > $10B

Below $10B, momentum captures noise — pump-and-dumps, illiquid stocks, micro-caps with unreliable data. Above $10B, momentum reflects genuine institutional capital flows and earnings-driven re-ratings. The $8–12B range was tested; $10B is the sweet spot.

EBIT > 0

Filters out money-losing companies. Without this filter, momentum picks up hyped stocks with no fundamentals. Removing the EBIT filter reduces Sharpe by 0.10–0.15 in testing.

MA250 regime filter

When the S&P 500 closes below its 250-day moving average, the strategy exits all stock positions. Without this filter, maximum drawdown exceeds −60%. With it, drawdown is contained to -41.9%. The MA250 is slower than MA200, which reduces whipsaws (false exits and re-entries).

GLD during bear months

Gold has near-zero correlation with the momentum strategy. During bear months, GLD averages positive returns. Holding GLD instead of cash adds approximately +4% CAGR without materially increasing drawdown. Before GLD inception (Nov 2004), bear months use gold futures (GC=F, scaled). Before Aug 2000, cash.

18th trading day signal, 19th trading day execution

Signal is computed after market close on the 18th trading day of each month (~day 26–27 of the calendar). Execution happens on the 19th trading day (~day 27–28). This ensures no look-ahead bias — the signal uses only past data, and trades are placed the following trading day.

XIV. Look-Ahead Bias Audit

Signal & Execution Timeline

18th trading day (signal): After market close (16:00 EST). All prices are known. Compute momentum using historical prices (126 and 252 trading days back). Check S&P 500 vs its 250-day moving average. All data is from the past. ✓

19th trading day (execution): Buy/sell at market open. Signal was computed the previous evening. No same-day execution. ✓

XV. Risks & Caveats

  • Transaction costs not included. Approximately 84 stock trades per year plus ~4 GLD rotations. Estimated impact: −0.5% to −1.0% CAGR.
  • Overfitting risk. Multiple parameter combinations were tested. Expect 20–30% Sharpe degradation in live trading.
  • 28 years, 3 bear markets. Includes the 2000–2003 dot-com bust, 2008 GFC, and 2020 COVID crash. Multiple regime types tested.
  • Concentration risk. 7 stocks at 14.3% each. A single-stock blowup costs ~14% of the portfolio.
  • Realistic expectation post-costs: CAGR +22–26%, Sharpe 0.75–0.90.
